crop.notes: The whole 'The Manly Art' article is in the clipping; a short unrelated Safe Deposit Company notice sits at the top.

ocr.notes: Gist is there but many garbled words and dropped lines (e.g. 'Bar llagher' for 'Bar Gallagher', 'old Bil De ip' for 'old Bill Davis', the 'Tom, you bloat' line).

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat reported that Allen and Ben Hogan signed articles at Looney & Herbert's saloon on September 25, 1873, to fight for $1,000 a side on October 28, the ground to be chosen later.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Friday, September 26, 1873'; not the Globe-Democrat until 1875.

facts.fact: Allen and Ben Hogan signed articles to fight a fair stand-up fight under the new rules for $1,000 a side on October 28, 1873, the ground to be picked by one man from each side; Arthur Chambers witnessed for Allen
places: Looney & Herbert's saloon, Sixth and St. Charles streets, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen refused Hogan's requests to leave the stake open and postpone the fight two weeks
facts.quote: Ben, all I want is a good square fight, and may the best man win.

facts.fact: Allen said he bore McCoole no ill will after their fight and had tried to visit him
facts.quote: I have no ill feeling again a man I fight. It's all a matter of business with me. I tried to get up stairs to see Mike, but they wouldn't let me.

facts.fact: Allen mentioned his wife, saying a false report of McCoole's death left her unable to sleep
facts.quote: Why the report reached us last night that Mike was dead, and my wife was in a terrible state. She couldn't sleep at all.

notes: The old summary's 'near Cincinnati' is not in the article. Allen said he would rest two weeks before training; his right second knuckle was slightly cut. He also rated Bill Davis's handwriting best among fighters.
